It is treated as a candidate shrine either for the Meishin-taisha Tsumatsuhime Shrine or for the two small shikinaisha Takatsumihiko and Takatsumihime shrines. Its former modern rank was village shrine. {{nihongo|'''Takatsumi Shrine'''|高積神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province}}.

The shrine has two sites on Mt. Takatsumi (237 m, also called Wasayama): the upper shrine on the summit and the lower shrine at the foot.

; Additional deities
* Amaterasu Omikami, Susanoo-no-Mikoto, Hachioji-no-kami
* Oyamazumi-no-kami, Ketsuwake-no-kami, Emperor Ojin
* Empress Jingu, Hime-no-Okami

== History ==
The foundation is unknown. One major theory identifies this shrine with "Tsumatsuhime Shrine" (Meishin-taisha) in the Engishiki; another identifies it with "Takatsumihiko" and "Takatsumihime" small shrines. The first record linked to Tsumatsuhime appears in the ''Shoku Nihongi'' (702), mentioning transfer of deities including Itakiso, Ooyatsuhime, and Tsumatsuhime.

The ''Shinsho Gecchokufu-sho'' (806) records endowments to "Tsumatobihime no Kami" in Kii. In the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' (927), "Tsumatsuhime Shrine, Meishin-taisha, monthly and niiname offerings" is listed in Nagusa District.

In a medieval water-rights dispute (1433) between Hinokuma/Kunikakasu shrines and Wasa estate, records claimed this shrine had ancient relocations and great authority. The ''Kii Zoku Fudoki'' considered identification with Tsumatsuhime highly plausible.

In 1873 it was ranked village shrine. In 1910, more than ten shrines in the Wasa area, including Keshizume Shrine, were merged into Takatsumi Shrine.

== Divine ranks ==
Records include elevations of deities identified as Tsumatsuhime, Takatsumihiko, and Takatsumihime in classical sources such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' and ''Kii no Kuni Jinmyocho''.
